title: Matrix-stripe quant paths & prefill pipeline to minimize dequant stalls
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce CPU/GPU stalls caused by late dequantization work during prefill and decode by introducing a matrix-stripe kernel abstraction and a prefill pipeline that staggers dequant work before attention compute. Problem: current mixed-precision runtime defers dequant until execution time which creates synchronization points and increases per-token tail latency for INT8/FP8 model paths. This ticket designs and implements a kernel selection path that allows matrix-stripe layouts to keep quantized data in compute-friendly chunks, schedules dequant as a low-priority prefill pass, and adds a fallback fast-path for short sequences.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end hosted API throughput for a 7B model on p4d/x86 with INT8 path improves tokens/sec by >= 18% vs baseline without hidden stalls
99th percentile decode latency reduced by >= 25ms on mixed sequence workloads (prefill-heavy) in our internal perf harness
No regression on float32 runtime paths; FP32 latencies within 3% of baseline
New kernel selection logic covered by unit tests and a runtime canary configured in Canary-Alpha in the console rollout
Design doc and microbenchmark results published to Confluence and linked in the ticket
decision_log: 2026-03-06: Choose matrix-stripe memory layout for intermediate GEMM output to improve coalesced loads when switching between quantized and dequantized kernels (decision by eng-runtime team)

2026-03-07: Use a two-stage prefill pipeline: stage 1 low-priority background dequantization into a KV-cache-ready buffer; stage 2 attention kernel consumes dequant buffers. This avoids blocking latency-critical decode threads.
2026-03-09: Prefer int8->fp16 dequant fast-path on A100-like hardware and int8->fp32 on older GPUs; add explicit kernel tags for hardware capability during selection.
2026-03-11: Keep an escape hatch that reverts to eager dequant if memory pressure exceeds threshold to avoid OOM on large-batch scenarios
benchmarks: Baseline (int8 mixed, no prefill pipeline): 12.4k tokens/sec, 99p decode latency 182ms (7B workload, batch=4, seq_prefill=128)
Matrix-stripe + staggered prefill (experimental): 14.7k tokens/sec (+18.5%), 99p decode latency 155ms (-27ms)
Short-seq fast-path (seq <= 32): no dequant path, tokens/sec 15.1k, 99p latency 142ms
FP32 path unchanged: 11.8k tokens/sec (within 2% of prior)
implementation_notes: Introduce kernel tag: kernel.layout = matrix_stripe; coordinate with compiler to emit block-stride GEMM loops
Add scheduler hook: prefill_scheduler.enqueue_dequant(buffer_id, priority=low) which runs on separate CUDA stream to overlap with I/O and tokenization
Modify KV cache API to accept 'ready' flags so attention kernels only read from dequantized buffers when available
Kernel selection logic: prioritize matrix_stripe-int8->fp16 where GPU supports native int8 tensor cores; fallback to int8->fp32 kernel on older sm architectures
Instrumentation: add per-token stall counters and a 'dequant_wait_ms' histogram to trace in console metrics
qa_steps: Run perf harness job runtime/perf/prefill/7B with scenarios: long-prefill (seq=512), mixed-prefill (seq random 1-512), short-prefill (seq<=32)
Smoke test on dedicated pool with mixed precision to validate no correctness drift (run evaluation prompts and compare logits against reference FP32 within tolerance)
Run memory-pressure test with concurrent large-batch requests to ensure OOM escape hatch triggers and falls back to eager dequant
Create canary rollout (Canary-Alpha) targeting 1% of traffic for 48 hours with logging enabled, check cost and latency dashboards
